questions.question: Which of the following metals is found in free state in nature?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The reactivity of a metal is defined as its tendency to undergo a chemical reaction, either with another material or by itself.
 
• Metals that have high reactivity readily react and therefore, cannot exist in a free state whereas metals with low reactivity can be found in a free state in nature.
 
• Following is the order of reactivity in metals from highest to lowest:

Potassium>Sodium>Calcium>Magnesium>Aluminium>Zinc>Iron>Tin>Lead>Hydrogen>Copper>Mercury>Silver>Gold

As can be seen, **copper has low reactivity**__ which is why__** it can exist in the free state**__ whereas sodium, potassium, and aluminium cannot since they have high reactivities.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments measures infra-red radiation?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

A **Bolometer **is a device for measuring the** power of incident electromagnetic radiation via the heating of a material with a temperature-dependent electrical resistance**. In this device, a resistive element is exposed to microwave power.

A dc bias current is applied to the resistor to raise its temperature via Joule heating, such that the resistance is matched to the waveguide characteristic impedance.

After applying microwave power, the bias current is reduced to return the Bolometer to its resistance in the absence of microwave power.

The change in the dc power is then equal to the absorbed microwave power

__**Explanation:**__

 Bolometer 
 It is used to measures heat and radiation of Microwave energy and infrared radiation.

 It is a is software that divides high dimensional single-cell data into subpopulations.

 It is a device that detects direct (normal incidence) solar beam radiation.

• Established on **12 July 1982**__, the __**National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**__ is a Development Financial Institution or Bank which mainly focuses on the rural sector of India.
 
• NABARD was founded on the recommendations B.Sivaraman Committee.
 
• It was established to implement the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act 1981.
 
• It is responsible for Policy Planning and Operations concerning agriculture and economic activities in rural areas.
 
• Its headquarters is in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

questions.question: Article ____________ of the Constitution of India provides special rights and privileges to permanent residents of Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.solution:
__
 
• This article is now obsolete and J&K is now a union territory.
 
• **Article 35A**__ of the Indian Constitution was given the __**power to the Jammu and Kashmir state's Legislature to define who can be the permanent residents of the State**__ and __**what special privileges and rights can be enjoyed by them**__.
 
• It was introduced under Article 370 of the Indian Constitution through The Constitution Order, 1954.
 
• Following are the privileges provided to the permanent residents as per Article 35A:
 
 
• Employment under the State Government.
 
• Ability to contest elections and vote.
 
• Ability to acquire immovable property and land in the State.
 
• Access to h
ealth care and higher education benefits.
 
• Right to scholarships and other such forms provided by the State Government.

questions.question: The first woman Secretary general of SAARC is from which country?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Maldivian diplomat Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed**__ was the first female __**Secretary-General of SAARC**__.
 
• She was appointed at the 33rd Session of the SAARC Council of Ministers in February 2011.
 
• She assumed the office in Kathmandu on 1 March 2011 and held the position till 24 January 2012. 
 
• The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) is an intergovernmental organization and union of South Asian states India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, Nepal, and the Maldives.
 
• This organization works towards promoting regional and economic integration among the countries involved.
